shapes.label: Distance in a free-fall interval
shapes.definition: A body falls from rest; the distance or ratio of distances covered in named seconds or intervals.

shapes.label: Position from a velocity equation
shapes.definition: v(t) is given as a polynomial; integrate for position or distance over an interval.

shapes.label: Velocity or acceleration from position equation
shapes.definition: The position x is given as an equation in time t, or time as an equation in x; differentiate to find the velocity or acceleration, or evaluate the average velocity between two times.

shapes.label: Distance in the nth second
shapes.definition: A body moves with constant acceleration; use the distance covered in a named second of its motion, or a ratio of such distances, to find another quantity of the motion.

shapes.label: Fall in two stages
shapes.definition: A body's vertical motion changes from one phase to another, such as acceleration into free flight or free fall into constant velocity; find the velocity or height linking the phases, then the time or another asked quantity.

shapes.label: A body thrown straight up
shapes.definition: A body is thrown vertically upward; find a height, time, speed, or distance at or between named times, taking into account whether it has already reached its highest point and started to fall back.

shapes.label: Zero velocity without zero acceleration
shapes.definition: A direct or assertion-reason question testing that a body having zero velocity at an instant does not mean it also has zero acceleration at that instant, as at the top of a vertical throw or the moment it reverses direction.

shapes.label: Basic equations of straight-line motion
shapes.definition: A body moves with constant acceleration along a straight line; given some of the initial velocity, final velocity, time, and distance, find the remaining quantity directly from the equations of motion.

shapes.label: Stopping distance in two parts
shapes.definition: A body decelerates uniformly and loses a stated fraction of its velocity while covering one distance, then covers a further distance before stopping; find the ratio of the two distances.
